notes:
Docket told a transit agency to delete the fields that let it send a cleaning crew.

Its "Report a Biohazard" form asks for the station, where on the platform, and which car — then your name and a way to reach you. Docket counted ten fields, decided that was a long enquiry form, and advised cutting it down: "for a first contact you usually need a name, one way to reach them, and what they need — the rest can be asked in the reply."

That advice is wrong here, and following it would do harm. The station and the car number are not friction, they are the whole point: without them nobody knows where to go. And there is no reply in which to ask, because most people filing that form never hear back and do not expect to.

The check was doing what it was built to do. Docket has always treated a long form as a conversion problem, because for a first-contact enquiry it is one — every extra field costs completions, and that finding has been right on plenty of sites. What it could not tell was that some forms are not first contact at all. It already knew this in two other places: a library's catalogue search is not an enquiry form, and neither is a comment box, and both were excluded years' worth of versions ago for exactly the same reason. An incident report is the third of that kind, and it is now excluded too.

**A form that reports something is not a form that asks for something.** Docket now recognises a page that exists so somebody can report a hazard, a fault or an incident — from the page saying so itself, in its title or heading — and leaves its fields alone. A page offering a free report is not one of those, and its form is still checked, because a lead magnet with fourteen fields is exactly the problem this was written for.

**Also: a running audit now tells you its own time limit.** If you ask Docket's local service how an audit is going, it reports how long the crawl has been running. Until now it did not report the limit that crawl was given, which made the first number hard to act on — forty minutes elapsed means something quite different against a one-hour budget than against a ten-minute one. Both are there now, side by side. This matters only if you drive Docket from a script or a dashboard rather than the app, since the app already knows what it asked for.
